For the Petitioner(s) : Mr. P. Mahanta, Advocate
 For the Respondent(s) : Mr C. Baruah, Cgc
 Ms. S. Baruah, Govt. Advocate
 Before
 Honourable Mr. Justice Devashis Baruah
 Order
Date : 11.11.2024 Heard Mr. P. Mahanta, the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners,

Mr. C. Baruah, the learned CGC appearing on behalf of the NHAI as well as the NHIDCL and Ms. S.
Baruah, the learned Government Advocate appears on behalf of the District Administration including the CALA.

2. The petitioners herein are aggrieved by the determination of compensation by the Competent Authority under Section 3G(1) of the National Highways Act, 1956 (for short 'the Act of 1956') on the grounds that the Competent Authority have not included the solatium interest as well as the other compensation components as stipulated in Schedule-I to Schedule-III of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act of 2013') which was made applicable for acquisition made under the National Highways Act, 1956.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. Mr. P. Mahanta, the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners Page No.# 5/6 submitted that the petitioners are entitled to the additional amounts taking into account the well settled principles of law laid down by the Supreme Court in the Case of National Highways Authority of India vs P. Nagaraju @ Cheluvaiah & Another reported in (2022) 15 SCC 1 and further submitted that in terms with Section 3G(7) of the Act of 1956, it was incumbent upon the Competent Authorities to determine the compensation as per law.

entities.text: National Highways Authority of India vs P. Nagaraju @ Cheluvaiah & Another reported in (2022) 15 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He therefore submitted that this is a fit case where this Court ought to exercise the writ jurisdiction in the instant proceedings.

4. Per contra Mr. C. Baruah, appearing on behalf of the NHAI as well as the NHIDCL submitted that if the petitioners are aggrieved with the compensation, the petitioners had the remedy under Section 3G(5) of the Act of 1956.
5. This Court has heard the learned counsels appearing on behalf of the parties and has also perused the materials on record.

This Court further takes note of Section 3G(5) of the Act of 1956 which Page No.# 1/6 vs The Union Of India And 5 Ors on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17426282/
4 categorically mandates that any of the parties to the proceedings being aggrieved as regard the determination of the quantum of compensation, the matter can be referred to the Arbitrator.
6. Consequently, this Court is not inclined to entertain the instant writ petition in view of the alternative and efficacious remedy available.

Accordingly, this Court therefore, disposes of the instant writ petition with a liberty to the petitioners to submit individual representation(s) to the Competent Authority, who, shall upon receipt of the same, shall forward the same to the Arbitrator appointed under Section 3G(5) of the Act of 1956.
7. In the said proceedings, the petitioner would be at liberty to raise all the issues as regards the inadequacy of the compensation on the basis of the well settled principles of law.
Page No.# 6/6 8.
With the above observations and directions the instant writ petition stands disposed of.
